A1.justification: Both complete, readable 24-page PDFs describe the same SnapViT research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; all pages except 1 and 11 render identically.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, classification and segmentation results, runtime measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original pruning experiments, classification and segmentation results, runtime measurements, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same self-supervised sensitivity scores, xNES optimization, elastic pruning procedure, and optional post-pruning processing. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven classification datasets and Pascal VOC 2012 segmentation tasks. Appendix E retains the same pruning-data comparisons involving ImageNet-1k, DiffusionDB, Shaders-21k, and merged evaluation-dataset samples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including LAMP, SNIP Magnitude, FPTP, SparseGPT, LLM Surgeon, and NViT. Table 1 also retains SN-Net, LPViT, and SA ViT.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–B retain identical splits, preprocessing, sparsity settings, model configurations, metrics, and evaluation procedures, including 20-neighbor classification and 100-epoch linear probing.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix E retain the same analyses of global interactions, optimization iterations, target sparsities, loss choice, pruning data, CKA initialization, model size, and dense representation quality.

E5.justification: Appendix C and Table 9 retain identical reporting of means and standard deviations across seeds 0, 13, and 42. No repeated-run information or uncertainty reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative segmentation examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SnapViT's 82.6% ImageNet-1k accuracy, and Table 3 retains 63.5% average k-NN accuracy when modeling FFN and attention-head interactions.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, Hessian approximations, pruning-score definitions, and derivations are identical. Equations 1–14 and Appendix B.1's complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about fast, label-free, retraining-free elastic pruning and evolutionary approximation of cross-network interactions.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the difficulty of pruning extensively pretrained models, the proposed explanation involving distributed representational knowledge, and Appendix E's discussion of limited capacity at high sparsity.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, baseline adaptations, hardware, runtime and compute budgets, and code/model access information remain identical. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The same 84 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to earlier pruning and elastic-inference methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: Page 11 adds a sentence acknowledging Cees G. M. Snoek's partial funding through Horizon Europe project ELLIOT, grant 101214398. Page 1 updates the arXiv version/date stamp; the remaining prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added acknowledgment slightly reflows the references on page 11. All 13 figures and 11 tables retain their content, formatting, captions, and placement; the remaining layout is unchanged apart from the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and updates the version/date stamp, with minor local reflow. The scientific content, empirical support, interpretations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—are unchanged, so these administrative edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
